userStories.title: S1.1b — The media-render API: check, render, voice, mix, concurrency
userStories.description: The service's HTTP API (aiohttp, like the worker). POST /render takes a composition bundle: the template's html/css, the variables, brand assets inlined as data: URIs (logo, font files), media inputs as presigned GET URLs to OUR storage only (the service refuses any other host — allowlist from config, never arbitrary URLs), and an audio plan (voice lines, music track id and window, SFX cues). It runs `hyperframes check` first and refuses with 422 carrying the lint/layout/contrast findings; otherwise renders (--quality delivery --fps 30) and returns a job id. GET /render/{id} reports status, the check report and timings; GET /render/{id}/output/{name} streams the file. POST /tts synthesises Kokoro lines (one WAV per line, returns durations; voice and speed parameters, default af_heart at 0.95). The mix is ffmpeg exactly as the reference: voice placed with adelay, music ducked by sidechaincompress (threshold 0.015, ratio 10, attack 10, release 420) at x0.6, SFX, loudnorm I=-14 TP=-1.5 LRA=11. Concurrency (owner, 2026-09-23): at most TWO renders at once overall and ONE per workspace; further jobs queue FIFO. Every limit and timeout is config.

userStories.description: Seed at boot, idempotently, the Socials marketplace package — all DATA, reusing the PRD-230 machinery. (1) Two marketplace agents on the Shopify pattern (core/seeds/seed_shopify_agents.py: real Agent rows owner_type='marketplace', custom_persona_prompt + use_custom_persona, skills by name, Composio apps via agent_app_assignments; boot-wired like load_seed_data.py:187-188) — NOT marketplace_items: the marketplace API lists and installs Agent rows only (api/marketplace.py list_items/install_item). 'Social Media Director' (slug social-media-director) plans content, writes per-channel copy, picks templates, drafts posts with sources, renders them and submits them for approval, and never publishes. 'Brand Designer' (slug brand-designer) builds and keeps the brand kit (the website via platform_web_fetch, the brand-kit suggestions, platform_update_brand_kit) and checks renders against it. Unlike the Shopify seeder, reconcile skill links on EVERY boot, so builtin skills synced after the first boot attach to the existing marketplace agents. Never attach instagram-curator, twitter-engager, linkedin-content-creator or html-to-png. userStories.description: D13 and the build prompt's money contract: estimate, then check the post's cap and the workspace's monthly cap, then submit, then book. Footage does this (modules/socials/recipes/footage.py:664-669: priced, one _check_caps over the total, inside the per-workspace footage window). Voice does none of it. modules/socials/recipes/voice.py speak() (:448-489) goes straight from the balance read to FISH_AUDIO_SYNTHESIZE_SPEECH / ELEVENLABS_TEXT_TO_SPEECH, one paid call per line; voice.py never imports media_caps (no check_caps, media_spend or MediaCapExceeded), and its caller modules/socials/render.py _voiced (:312-337) checks nothing either. api/socials.py render_post (:456-509) resolves the voice plan for AVAILABILITY only (voice_recipes.plan_for). So a workspace whose socials.media_monthly_cap_usd is already spent, or set to 0 to forbid paid media, still pays Fish Audio (its API credit is dollars, voice.py:151-152) on every render with a Fish Audio voice, and ElevenLabs characters (the customer's plan) are booked at $0 (voice.py:27, _book :424-445), so no cap ever sees them. An agent reaches it: platform_create_social_post / platform_update_social_post take voice (modules/tools/discovery/actions_socials.py:105) and render by default. Every render re-speaks every line (no reuse, unlike footage slots), so a retry after a failed check pays again. The one booking voice does make is also not durable: _book is called on the event loop (voice.py:483), UsageTracker.track is @off_loop (core/llm/usage_tracker.py:221), so the row is handed to the best-effort threads and returns at once; the next cap check can run before it lands, and when the pool has no free connection within BEST_EFFORT_POOL_WAIT_S (2 s) the write is DROPPED with a warning (core/best_effort.py:55-64): spend without a booking. Footage avoids exactly this with await asyncio.to_thread(_book_rows, ...) (footage.py:643).
acceptanceCriteria: Before the first line is spoken, a toolkit voice render is priced: the script's units (Fish Audio: UTF-8 bytes; ElevenLabs: characters, the recipe's existing units) times a per-toolkit price per unit declared in orchestrator/config.py (no inline literal; add each new name to orchestrator/reports/config-surface.json). The price is checked with media_caps.check_caps against the post's cap and the workspace's monthly cap, inside a per-workspace window shared with footage (the modules/socials/recipes/toolkit.window pattern), so a render's footage and voice are checked against one running total and two renders cannot both spend the same remaining cap. Over either cap, NOTHING is spoken: the render fails with code voice_refused (or the footage refusal's code) and a message naming the cap, what was spent and what the voice would cost; no Composio speech call is made.

Every voice booking is written before speak() returns and before the window releases: _book runs through await asyncio.to_thread(...) (inline write, as footage.py:643 does), never directly on the event loop. ElevenLabs is booked at its priced amount (units x the configured price), not a hard-coded $0; Fish Audio still books its balance difference and, when the balance after cannot be read, books the priced amount (never $0) with the error recorded.

userStories.title: [HIGH] Concurrent renders all pass the monthly render quota: it counts only finished renders, so a workspace renders far past its plan's minutes
userStories.description: core/media_render_quota.py enforce_render_quota (:161-170) reads only the seconds already booked on the media lane (render_seconds_used :84-99), and a render books its seconds only when it has finished (modules/socials/render.py:606-611, on the needs_approval path; modules/documents/generation_service.py:651-656, after render_to_file). Nothing reserves the minutes of a render in flight and nothing serializes the check per workspace, so N renders requested before the first one finishes all read the same total and all start. Every render path shares the check: api/socials.py:492 render_post (POST /api/socials/posts/{id}/render and the platform_create_social_post / platform_update_social_post tools, whose render defaults to true) and generation_service.py:626 generate_social (POST /api/documents/generate, the template preview, the generate_document tool, the Playbook generate_document step and the mission coordinator). The design lets ONE render cross the line (media_render_quota.py:24-26); concurrency makes it N. Failure: a Basic workspace (10 minutes) with nothing used requests 20 renders of a 3-minute composition (MEDIA_RENDER_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS 180) within a few seconds, by REST or an agent drafting 20 posts: all 20 pass and up to 60 minutes are rendered and booked, repeatable every time the backlog drains. In normal use, the Weekly social posts Playbook drafts 5 posts that render at once. The render-seconds booking itself is also not durable: book_render_seconds (media_render_quota.py:173-178) is called on the event loop (render.py:611, generation_service.py:651), UsageTracker.track is @off_loop, so the row is written later on the best-effort threads, and it is DROPPED when no pool connection frees within BEST_EFFORT_POOL_WAIT_S (core/best_effort.py:55-64): a dropped row is minutes the quota never counts. The platform already solved this for Auto Live minutes: modules/voice/voice_meter.py counts reserved minutes (MeterReading.committed_minutes = ended_minutes + reserved_minutes).
acceptanceCriteria: A render reserves its seconds (the composition's declared duration) before media-render is called, and the quota compares booked seconds PLUS the seconds reserved by this workspace's renders in flight: a render starts only while booked + reserved < quota. The check and the reservation happen under one per-workspace lock that holds across uvicorn workers (a Postgres advisory lock, the modules/socials/recipes/toolkit.window pattern, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the workspace row). The reservation is released when the render ends: done (replaced by the booked seconds), failed, refused, timed out, or reaped at boot; one that is never released expires with the render's deadline (SOCIALS_RENDER_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS). Both render_post and generate_social use it. No new table unless an existing one cannot hold the reservation (say which in the commit body).

The refusal message still names the plan and the minutes used, and adds the minutes held by renders in progress. Enterprise and the local edition still have no quota (test_the_local_edition_renders_past_any_count and test_the_quota_a_workspace_gets unchanged and green).

userStories.title: [HIGH] One workspace can fill media-render's admission bound and lock every other workspace out of rendering
userStories.description: services/media-render/media_render/server.py post_render (:177-183) answers 503 busy when state.store.active_count() >= max_active_jobs. active_count (media_render/jobs.py:141-142) counts every unfinished job of EVERY workspace, and max_active_jobs defaults to 20 (media_render/config.py:215). The per-workspace limit lives only in the render lane (media_render/lanes.py: one rendering at a time per workspace), not at admission, and a job counts as active the moment it is accepted, before it reaches a lane. Railway runs ONE replica (infrastructure/railway-manifest.json media-render replicas 1). So one workspace with 20 renders in flight (checking, queued or rendering) holds every admission slot: every other workspace's POST /render gets 503, its orchestrator retries (core/media_render_client.submit_when_free) until the render's deadline (SOCIALS_RENDER_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS 1500 s) and then the post fails; the greedy workspace's own backlog drains one render at a time, at up to 180 s each (MEDIA_RENDER_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS). The owner's rule (2026-09-23): two renders at once overall, one per workspace, the rest QUEUED. Here the rest of the platform is refused.
